document.title: Excerpt from Statement of the Soviet Military Command in Afghanistan on the Withdrawal of Soviet Troops, February 14, 1989
document.authors: Soviet Military Command in Afghanistan / USSR Defense Ministry
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan: Lessons from the Last War
document.note: Statement delivered to the head of the UN Mission on the day the last Soviet soldier left. It reviews Soviet-Afghan relations, justifies the intervention, criticizes U.S. arming of the opposition in disregard of the Geneva agreements, and rejects Vietnam comparisons. Source: Lyakhovsky, Appendix 11.

events.description: Soviet Military Command in Afghanistan issues a statement on the completed withdrawal of Soviet troops. It rejects the Vietnam analogy and says the withdrawal followed the Geneva Agreements.
Withdrawal of Soviet forces from Afghanistan carried out according to plan under the Geneva Agreements. Property worth over 830 million rubles was transferred to the Afghan side.
Geneva Agreements on Afghanistan, which set the terms of the Soviet withdrawal. The year is not given in the text and is inferred.
The Soviet Military Command in Afghanistan issues a statement on the withdrawal of Soviet troops. It rejects comparisons with the US in Vietnam and says the withdrawal follows the Geneva Agreements.
Soviet forces withdraw from Afghanistan in accordance with the Geneva Agreements, and property worth over 830 million rubles is transferred to the Afghan side.
The Geneva Agreements on Afghanistan are cited as the framework governing the Soviet withdrawal. The text gives no signing date.

relationships.quote: nobody had invited the Americans in Vietnam

sources_cited: Alexander Lyakhovsky, Tragedy and Valor of Afghan, Iskon, Moscow 1995, Appendix 11
key_claims: The Soviet command rejects the analogy with US actions in Vietnam and describes the Soviet presence as invited by the legitimate Afghan government.
The command says the withdrawal was planned and carried out under the Geneva Agreements, in contrast to an American 'flight' from Vietnam.
The Soviets claim to have transferred property worth over 830 million rubles to the Afghan people during the withdrawal.
The command says it sought to prevent the last Soviet soldier's departure from starting a civil war, and pledges continued support for a political settlement.
